title: Delete MemoryIndex (dead code carrying live race risk)
description:
P2: `MemoryIndex` has a real, unguarded race condition (plain `Dictionary`, `Clear()`-then-refill `Rebuild()`) but **zero production consumers**. The three dictionaries (`ById`, `ByTag`, `ByReference`) are maintained on every Create/Update/Delete but never read by any code path outside tests. All search paths use `_store.LoadAll()`. This is dead weight carrying a latent concurrency bug that escalates to CRITICAL the moment search is wired to consult the index.

Scope:
- Remove `MemoryIndex.cs` class
- Remove DI registration from `MemorySmithStorageSetup.cs`
- Remove `_index` field from `MemoryApplicationService.cs`
- Update any tests that reference `MemoryIndex` directly
- Verify: full test pass, no regression in search or CRUD operations

Evidence: MemorySmith-Audit-20260702.md §1.4, MemorySmith-Audit-Delta-5-20260702.md §2, council/audit-synthesis-council-20260705.md

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 6-seat council audit synthesis. Retrieval Specialist ("delete it"), Data Model Architect ("dead weight"), and Skeptical Reviewer (LOW severity) all converge on deletion. No dissent.
